222:def equivalent(first: T, second: T) -> bool:
223:    """Compare two objects for equivalence (identity or equality), using
224:    array_equiv if either object is an ndarray. If both objects are lists,
225:    equivalent is sequentially called on all the elements.
226:    """
227:    # TODO: refactor to avoid circular import

231:        return True
232:    if isinstance(first, np.ndarray) or isinstance(second, np.ndarray):
233:        return duck_array_ops.array_equiv(first, second)
234:    if isinstance(first, list) or isinstance(second, list):
235:        return list_equiv(first, second)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
236:    return (first == second) or (pd.isnull(first) and pd.isnull(second))  # type: ignore[call-overload]
